text: IN: the Counterparty entity with its embedded PostalAddress and Contact beans, its search screen and edit form, and the lifecycle draft → active → retired.

comments.text: The lifecycle draft → active → retired is declared in scope, but no requirement or criterion says which transitions are allowed. Can a draft go straight to retired? Can a retired counterparty be reopened to active? The bean table carries default(draft) but nothing pins the transition graph, so two implementations could both satisfy the spec while behaving differently on the screen. Add a requirement stating the permitted transitions (e.g. draft → active, active → retired, retired terminal) and a criterion that verifies an out-of-order transition is rejected.

text: A1 (verifies P1): WHEN a counterparty's parent is set, directly or through a chain, to one of its own descendants, the system SHALL reject the change and leave the parent chain unchanged.

comments.text: A1 covers setting the parent to a descendant, but not the boundary case of setting a counterparty's parent to itself. Whether self counts as 'one of its own descendants' is ambiguous; if it doesn't, a one-node cycle slips past the only criterion verifying P1. Either state in P1/A1 that parent = self is also rejected, or add a criterion for it.

text: The lifecycle declares a retired state, but nothing in the spec says what retirement changes.

comments.text: Reviewer question: may a retired counterparty still be selected as another counterparty's parent, and may its row still be edited after retirement? Answered in Scope: retirement is a state of the register, not a behavioural gate at this stage — a retired counterparty may still be edited and may still be picked as a parent.

text: IN: retirement is a state of the register, not a behavioural gate at this stage — a retired counterparty may still be edited and may still be picked as another counterparty's parent; only its visibility as live business counterparties changes.

comments.text: This scope line promises that retirement changes a retired counterparty's "visibility as live business counterparties", but no section says what that change concretely is — is it a default filter on the search screen, a marker on the row, exclusion from some future list? Nothing verifies it either, so an implementation could satisfy the whole spec while the promised visibility change never appears. Either define the visibility effect (e.g. "the search screen defaults to excluding retired rows, with a filter to include them") with a criterion, or drop the clause and state that retirement is purely a status label at this stage.
